test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Manjit borrowed an amount of ₹2,20,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Manjit after 2 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Annual Rates = 7.5% − 3.5% = 4%

Difference in interest for 2 years = 4% × 2 = 8%

Required difference = 8% of ₹2,20,000

Difference = 0.08 × 2,20,000 = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2,20,000

Rate of Bank A (R₁) = 3.5% | Rate of Bank B (R₂) = 7.5%

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02eb92b196e8a5c89fce46e20155bef9e4197fea1702adeec80dbaada49260b9.png] 

⇒ SI from Bank A = (2,20,000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SIA = 2,200 × 7 = ₹15,400

⇒ SI from Bank B = (2,20,000 × 7.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SIB = 2,200 × 15 = ₹33,000

⇒ Difference = SIB − SIA = 33,000 − 15,400

⇒ Difference = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) Difference Formula

When Principal (P) and Time (T) are constant, the difference in interest is: ΔSI = (P × ΔR × T) ÷ 100, where ΔR is the difference in interest rates.

SI vs CI for First Year

For the first year, if the interest is compounded annually, the Simple Interest and Compound Interest on the same principal and rate are always equal.

SI and CI Difference for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by: CI − SI = P(R ÷ 100)².
